prompt: Inside a grand marble bank hall at midnight in 1926, the round vault door has just been blown off its hinges and smoke pours from the dark opening. A thin, white-haired man of about seventy-five, clean-shaven, hollow cheeks, dark bowler, stands close to a long lens at eye level, his head and shoulders filling the left half of the frame, three-quarter front, staring across the room. One hand holds a Thompson far out at his side, muzzle to the ceiling. Green glass desk lamps along the bent brass teller grilles light his face and lips emerald; a crimson alarm bulb above the vault rims his ear and colours the smoke. The polished floor doubles it all, green pools and a red smear, scattered notes lying blurred and unreadable upon it. Thanks.
